title: Derived tensor product and derived internal hom
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme. Let $\mathcal A$ be a closed symmetric monoidal Grothendieck abelian
category whose tensor product is additive and which has functorial flat resolutions. Let
$\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring] with pulled-back
ring object $\Lambda_X=p_X^*\Lambda$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. The derived
categories are those of [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories].

- **Layer A.** $D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal A)$ is monoidal for the *derived tensor
  product* $-\otimes^{\mathrm L}-$. This is the left derived functor, in two variables,
  of the tensor product of complexes of sheaves [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor], computed by
  replacing an argument by a K-flat resolution. The localization functor from complexes
  is lax monoidal.
- **Layer B.** $D(\Mod_{\Lambda_X})$ is monoidal for $-\otimes^{\mathrm L}_{\Lambda_X}-$.
  This is the two-variable K-flat derived functor of the *relative* tensor product
  $\otimes_{\Lambda_X}$ of module objects [def-sfb-modobj-relative-tensor], not a derived
  tensor product over $\mathbf Z$ followed by a quotient.
- **Internal hom.** Both monoidal structures are closed. The *derived internal hom* is
  *defined* as the internal hom of this closed structure. It is a bifunctor
  $\RHom(-,-)\colon D^{\mathrm{op}}\times D\to D$ with
  $K\otimes^{\mathrm L}-\dashv\RHom(K,-)$ for every $K$, naturally in $K$. Likewise there
  is $\RHom_{\Lambda_X}$ with
  $K\otimes^{\mathrm L}_{\Lambda_X}-\dashv\RHom_{\Lambda_X}(K,-)$.

proof.text: For layer A, take the tensor bifunctor defined in [def-sfb-derived-tensor-sheaves]. Its statement identifies this as the tensor of the monoidal structure of [lem-sfb-derived-monoidal] on $D(\Sh(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal A))$. Thus this is the specified K-flat derived monoidal structure, not an arbitrary monoidal structure on the same category. The computation and lax monoidal localization in [lem-sfb-derived-monoidal] apply to this very structure: writing $Q$ for localization to this derived category, for complexes $K,L$, replace $K$ by a K-flat complex $P$ with a quasi-isomorphism $P\to K$ to compute the product as $Q(P\otimes L)$; replacing $L$ instead gives the other allowed computation. The universal property in both variables, with the localization structure map, is stated specifically for these sheaves in [lem-sfb-derived-tensor-sheaves-derived].

For layer B, use the condensed-ring/scheme particular case explicitly stated in [def-sfb-derived-tensor-modules], with $R=\Lambda_X$ and $\mathcal C=\Sh(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab)$. It supplies the derived monoidal structure for this precise module category and identifies it as the structure of [lem-sfb-derived-monoidal] for the relative module-object tensor. That underived tensor is the balancing coequalizer of [def-sfb-modobj-relative-tensor]. Apply the computation asserted for this specified derived structure in [lem-sfb-derived-monoidal]: writing $Q$ for localization to this module derived category, its product is $Q(P\otimes_{\Lambda_X}L)$ for a relative K-flat resolution $P\to K$. The two-variable derived universal property for this same relative tensor is [lem-sfb-derived-tensor-modules-derived]. Thus the bifunctor being derived is already $\otimes_{\Lambda_X}$, as required.

Use [def-sfb-derived-hom-sheaves] and [def-sfb-derived-hom-modules]. Their statements specify closed monoidal structures on the exact derived categories and tensor products selected in steps 1 and 2, and define the derived internal homs as their internal hom bifunctors. In each displayed domain the first factor is the opposite of the derived category and the second is the derived category itself. Hence these are precisely the required contravariant/covariant bifunctors with values in the same derived category. This uses the structures asserted by those statements; it does not infer closedness from an arbitrary localization of an underived internal hom.

Use the parameter adjunctions of [def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom-adjunction-sheaves] and [def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom-adjunction-modules]. Evaluating each parameter adjunction at an object $K$ gives $K\otimes^{\mathrm L}-\dashv\RHom(K,-)$ and $K\otimes^{\mathrm L}_{\Lambda_X}-\dashv\RHom_{\Lambda_X}(K,-)$, respectively. Naturality in $K$ is precisely the parameter naturality already asserted by those statements, so this gives the required adjunctions for every $K$.

proof_origin.place: paragraphs 2–3, using the general monoidal structure specified in paragraph 1
